## Claims
- [computed] For \(Q=J_{2,4}/A_+J_{2,4}\), quotient free ranks in degrees \(4,\ldots,24\) are
  \[
  (1,1,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0),
  \]
  i.e. \(1,1,2,1,1\) in degrees \(4,5,6,7,8\) and \(0\) in degrees \(9,\ldots,24\); every torsion-factor list is empty. [artifact baf9447fe15327ded6640cbb3b0b3c7b43b62cdb3fb6fa1afcb78fe218ca5d97]
- [proved] Using the accepted interval presentation (supported only in degrees \(4,\ldots,24\)) and accepted identification of the complete \(A_+J_{2,4}\) Pieri-row lattice, the preceding Smith data give
  \[
  J_{2,4}/A_+J_{2,4}\cong
  \mathbb Z^{1+1+2+1+1}\cong\mathbb Z^6.
  \]
- [source-backed] The supplied source summary states that Theorem 5.4 provides two generating sets for \(J_v\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), each of cardinality \(\binom{a+b}{a}\). [source-6, lines 14-42]
- [proved] For \(i=j=p=c=2\), \(a=b=2\), so each accepted generating family has \(\binom42=6\) elements. Since each maps to a surjection \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow J_{2,4}/A_+J_{2,4}\cong\mathbb Z^6\), accepted indexed-family Nakayama implies that both
  \[
  \{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\}
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}
  \]
  map to \(\mathbb Z\)-bases of the quotient. Hence neither has a proper subfamily generating \(J_{2,4}\).
- [proved] The requested target is established: both listed families are minimal generating sets of \(J_{2,4}\). No broader minimality claim is concluded.

## Strategy
Extract the accepted Smith data, sum its torsion-free degreewise ranks, then apply accepted generation and indexed-family Nakayama.

None for this \(c=4\) corollary relative to the accepted interval, generation, Nakayama, and computation inputs.
